Below are high-level economics to give you a sense; I’ve attached an updated workbook with worked examples at 50M and 60M tokens and a simple Dedicated sizing estimate. These are examples 

High-level pricing examples (illustrative)
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): $0.0006 per token (input + output). At 50M tokens = $30,000/month. Easy to start, no infra commitment, regional controls (US) and standard audit logs.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly reserved fee for a GPU pool + lower per-token compute (or included in commit). Example: a 2-GPU reserved pool for your workload (handles sustained ~350–450 QPS for short prompts) = $38,000/month reserved commit + lower variable egress/ops fees.
- Private VPC / On-prem: one-time onboarding + infra integration fee (~$120k–$200k depending on on-prem complexity) + monthly platform/support (~$10k–$25k) plus customer-managed infra costs. Best when strict PHI/on-prem rules require full isolation.

Bursting & autoscale notes:
- Dedicated can be configured with burst credits and autoscaling policies; bursts beyond reserved capacity are billed at an overage rate or via a short-term burst pool. We recommend a small buffer (20–30%) if you have spiky windows.

Procurement / timeline:
- Hosted: 1–2 weeks (SLA add-ons take longer)
- Dedicated: 6–8 weeks (procurement + reserved capacity provisioning)
- Private: 8–14 weeks (depends on network/infra approvals)

I’ll prepare a formal quote and SKU-level numbers once you confirm: 1) monthly token target (50M vs 60M) and 2) whether PHI requires on-prem. I’ve looped Neha (solutions) to validate dedicated sizing and Marissa to own commercial terms.
